text:
Aya: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A about APAC capacity and autoscaler behavior. Dropping concise answers + action items.
Marcus: Bottom line: APAC pilot next week. We're prioritizing Reserved pools for enterprise parity; Burst (spot) for Hosted optional.
Ravi: Which regions exactly? SYD primary, BOM sibling; we’ll add SIN/TOK in wave 2. Decision was procurement + peering.
Sophie: Explain burst impact: burst is a spot-backed shared pool for Hosted only. It never reclaims Dedicated reservations.
Marcus: If spot is evicted mid-request: we attempt a drain (15-20s), snapshot KV-cache; if eviction is abrupt request returns 502 with trace id and autoscaler retries to fallback.
Aya: Fallback order we agreed: 1) local Reserved, 2) local Burst, 3) sibling APAC, 4) EU, 5) US. Cross-region require org opt-in.
Ravi: Data residency controls?
Sophie: Route flag `residency_mode: strict|preferred`. If strict, autoscaler will NOT route cross-region and will return 429 with header `x-rdi-reason: residency-block`.
Marcus: Billing: no surprise egress. Console will show projected cross-region egress and require opt-in for auto-failover; we'll also emit alerts when burst spend > threshold.
Sophie: Cold-start SLOs: node provision target <= 120s in some APAC regions; model warm-up median: ~20s (7B), ~40s (13B), ~80s (70B). We pre-warm top variants.
Aya: Action items: (1) API: add `residency_mode` enum + error header text (owner: @eng-api) by Fri, (2) Console: surface cross-region estimate & opt-in (owner: @console) next sprint, (3) SRE: tag cold-start telemetry with region+variant (owner: @sre).
deploy-bot: Canary for autoscaler v1.2 started -> 5% traffic.
Ravi: Tiny doc ask: one-paragraph FAQ "What happens on spot eviction?" and SDK sample for `residency_mode`.
Aya: Will compile PR links + FAQ and post in #product-update before EOD. Ping me for any follow-ups.
